note: Anchors, labels and the read order are rendered from rubric.json `definition` at run time (lib/rubrics/engines/consult-llm.ts systemPrompt).
rules: Read the stay record only: the pre-operative indication, the theatre record, the discharge, then the numbered outpatient follow-up records. Nothing else is known.
Label the STAY, not the person. The first outpatient visit after discharge counts only when it is about the same problem as the operation.
Silence, or no same-problem record, is never positive: answer unscored.

negative_signals uses ONLY these codes: ssi_pus (pus or a surgical-site infection; expected serous drainage is not), fever, spreading_redness, return_to_theatre (an unplanned return or revision), complication_documented (a same-problem visit that documents a complication). Answer [] when none is documented.
planned_staging is true only when the record states that a further operation or dressing stage was PLANNED; a planned stage is not a negative.
same_problem: one boolean per numbered follow-up record, in order: true when that record is about the problem the operation treated.
better_or_no_complaint is true only when a same-problem follow-up record documents no complaint, or the patient symptomatically better; expected symptoms do not veto.
escalate is true when the fork is wound versus expected drainage, or staging versus a return to theatre, and you cannot tell.
The label is a proposal: positive needs a same-problem record with no complaint or better and no negative signal; negative needs at least one code.
Every evidence quote is copied EXACTLY from the stay record; never paraphrase.
Answer with ONE JSON object and nothing else.
user_header: STAY RECORD. Dates are days after the admission or after the discharge. Follow-up records are numbered R1, R2, ... in time order.
